transcript.text: hoover washer drier showing EO3 wont drain, ive done the filter its clean. H3DS4965DACE. pump just buzzes. do i need a new pump??

Not necessarily. A buzzing pump with E03 often means the pump is fine but jammed or blocked. The motor is getting power but can't turn. Check these first, since they're free:

Before you start: unplug the machine and have towels and a shallow tray ready, as there will likely still be water in it.

### 1. Check the impeller (most common cause)
• Remove the filter again and shine a torch into the hole behind it.
• You should see the pump impeller (little plastic vanes). Poke it gently with a finger or the handle of a wooden spoon.
• Normal: it turns with a slightly "notchy" or magnetic feel and a bit of play.
• Stiff or won't turn: something's caught, such as hair, a hair grip, a coin, a bra wire, or fluff wrapped round it. Fish it out with fingers or long-nose pliers.
• Spins totally freely with no resistance, or the vanes are broken: the pump has likely failed.

### 2. Check the drain hose and outlet
• Pull the machine out and make sure the hose isn't kinked or squashed behind it.
• If it goes into a sink trap spigot, check the trap isn't blocked. If the sink plumbing was recently changed, check the blanking disc in the spigot was cut out.
• Quick test: take the hose off the waste, put the end in a bucket, and run a drain/spin.

### 3. Sump hose (if the above are clear)
There's a rubber hose between the bottom of the drum and the pump. Small socks can get stuck in it. Getting to it usually means removing the front kickplate or tipping the machine back, so it's a bit more work.

### If it is the pump
• A replacement drain pump for Hoover/Candy machines is usually around £15–£35. Search your model number (H3DS4965DACE) or the part number printed on the old pump.
• It's a fairly easy DIY job for most people: a couple of screws, two hose clips, and a wiring plug.
• An engineer callout would typically cost £80–£120 or more including the part.

Bottom line: if the impeller won't turn, clear it and you'll probably be sorted. If it turns freely and the hoses are clear but it still just buzzes, then yes, it's time for a new pump.

did the impeller check. spins totally freely, no resistance at all, feels like its not connected to anything. torch shows one fin looks snapped. hose is disconnected and clear and sink waste is clear too. so pump is knackered right?

Yes, that's a failed pump. Spinning freely with no resistance plus a snapped fin means the impeller has broken or come loose from the motor. The motor turns (hence the buzz) but nothing moves the water. Since your hose and waste are clear, a replacement pump should fix it.

### Getting the right part
• Best option: once the old pump is out, check the label on it for the part number and match that exactly.
• Otherwise: search "H3DS4965DACE drain pump" on a parts site (e.g. eSpares, Partmaster, 4washerparts) and confirm the plug type and shape match.
• On many Hoover/Candy machines you can buy either the motor only (it twists or clips off the filter housing) or the full pump with housing. Motor-only is cheaper if your housing is in good condition.
• Expect roughly £15–£35.

### Rough steps
1. Unplug the machine and turn off the water.
2. Drain any remaining water through the filter into a tray, with towels down.
3. Remove the kickplate (bottom front panel), usually clips or a couple of screws.
4. Undo the screws holding the filter housing to the front of the machine.
5. Remove the pump. Depending on the version, it's usually a twist-off or a couple of screws or a clip from the filter housing.
6. Take a photo of the wiring, then pull off the connector.
7. If replacing the full assembly, loosen the hose clips and swap the hoses over.
8. Fit the new pump, reconnect everything, and run a rinse and spin to check for leaks.

If the pump is hard to reach from the front, tilting the machine back (with help, as it's heavy) usually gives access from underneath.

### Important tip
Find the snapped fin piece. It's probably loose in the filter housing or sump. If you leave it in, it can jam or wreck the new pump straight away. Check inside the housing and the hose ends while everything's apart.
